0.0.n: The て-form of 見る is used alone here as a casual request.

1.0.n: This noun names the body of water where the town floats.

1.1.n: This particle marks where the town floats; English uses on here.

1.2.n: The plain form directly describes 町, specifying which kind of town it is.

1.3.n: This noun is described by the preceding 海に浮かぶ.

1.4.n: This sentence-ending particle draws the listener’s attention; directly after a noun, it has a feminine conversational feel.

2.0.n: The speaker refers to herself; the topic-marking particle は is left out in this casual introduction.

2.2.n: This is the speaker’s name, written in katakana.

2.3.n: This polite ending completes the speaker’s introduction.

0.tip: A verb’s て-form can stand alone as a casual request.

1.lit: Sea-on floating town, I tell you!
1.tip: 海に浮かぶ comes before 町 to describe it: a town floating on the sea.

2.tip: In speech, 私 can introduce the topic without は, while です keeps the introduction polite.
